question: does a boundary observation always belong to the request that issued it, under pool pressure?
design: pool max is far below concurrency so nearly every query is queued and dispatched from a foreign request's stack, which is the exact condition that produced the defect
single_variable: the two arms differ in exactly one file, src/capture/patch-pg.mjs; every other file is identical

defect.mechanism: a queued pg pool connection request is dispatched synchronously from the stack of whichever request RELEASES a connection, so AsyncLocalStorage reports the releasing request context and the nested Client.query records into a foreign incident
consequences: correctness: a captured incident contains boundary events it did not issue
privacy: SQL parameters and result rows of a request that was NEVER selected can be persisted into another request incident
nondeterminism: contamination is load- and timing-dependent
defect.fix: bind the caller capture context to the pool connect callback so the observation belongs to the issuing request whatever dispatches it

findings.description: unselected request markers never appear in any captured incident
each incident contains only its own request marker
two concurrently-captured incidents never exchange boundary observations
no incident contains markers from both armed routes
